What's included

The things that actually change a holiday

No line items, no surprises at checkout. Every stay at ZO carries all six of these.

Airport pickup, on us

Dabolim or Mopa, any hour. Send us your flight number and a driver with your name on a board will be waiting past the gate.

Infinity pool over the sand

28 metres of it, heated in monsoon, open 6am to 10pm. Towels, shade and a poolside menu that runs all day.

A kitchen with no freezer

Chef Reshma buys at the Candolim market at 6am. Xacuti, ambot-tik, rechado — cooked the way her grandmother wrote it down.

Cancellation that means it

Free cancellation up to 24 hours before arrival. No card charge until you check in, and no resort fee ever.

Scooters at reception

Serviced Activas and two Royal Enfields, helmets included, ₹400 a day. Insured, papers in the seat, fuelled before you leave.

Wi-Fi you can work on

300 Mbps fibre with a diesel backup, plus three shaded work decks and a small meeting room for six.

Our specialities

Five things only ZO has

Candolim has plenty of hotels with a pool and a view. These are the reasons people book this one.

“We don't sell rooms. We sell the fortnight you'll talk about for a year.”

Reshma & Ivan D'Souza · Owners since 2011

  • The Azulejo Wing

    Six heritage rooms built around original 1908 Portuguese tilework, restored panel by panel with a conservator from Margao. Room 104's wall is the oldest surviving in Candolim.

  • Susegad Suppers

    A fourteen-seat chef's table every Saturday under the mango tree. Seven courses, one long table, and the fish chosen that morning. Guests eat free once per stay.

  • Our own sunset boat

    The Maria Bela leaves our jetty at 5:10pm daily — dolphins, the Aguada headland, and a flask of solkadhi. Twelve guests, no other operators, no hard sell.

  • Salt & Til spa

    Four Kerala-trained therapists and oils pressed in Ponda. Abhyanga, post-swim salt scrubs, and a 7am yoga shala on the roof that costs nothing to attend.

  • Plastic-free since 2019

    Glass and copper in every room, filtered water on tap, a rainwater tank under the courtyard, and solar for 60% of our load. We publish the numbers each April.

FAQ

Asked before you arrive

What are the check-in and check-out times?

Check-in from 2pm, check-out by 11am. Early arrivals can use the pool, showers and breakfast room while the room is made up, and we'll hold your bags for free either side. Late checkout to 4pm is complimentary when the room isn't turning over — just ask the night before.

Is the airport transfer really included?

Yes, one arrival pickup and one departure drop per booking, from either Dabolim (GOI, 45 km) or Mopa / Manohar (GOX, 38 km). Send your flight number at least 12 hours ahead. Extra trips are ₹1,600 to Dabolim and ₹1,400 to Mopa.

How far is the beach, honestly?

Three minutes on foot — 220 metres down a lane and through the coconut grove, no road to cross. We keep a stack of towels and a cooler by the gate, and our beach shack partner holds two loungers for ZO guests until 4pm daily.

What's the cancellation policy?

Free cancellation up to 24 hours before check-in on every rate, including villas. Cancel inside 24 hours and one night is charged. No-shows are charged the first night. Monsoon bookings (June–September) can be moved once, free, up to the day of arrival.

Are children and pets welcome?

Children of any age, yes — cots are free, and under-6s eat free from the main menu. The pool has a 60 cm shallow end and a lifeguard from 9am to 6pm. Well-behaved dogs stay free in the Garden Courtyard rooms and villas; they're welcome everywhere except the pool deck and breakfast room.

How do we pay, and is there a resort fee?

No resort fee, no service charge, no charge for the car. We take UPI, all major cards, and cash in rupees at reception. Nothing is charged when you book — your card is held and settled at checkout, with GST included in every price you see on this page.

The Smell of Wet Earth

Most people visit Goa chasing the sun. The ones who love it best arrive when the sky opens up.

4 min read · The ZO Journal

Monsoon in Goa is not an inconvenience to hide from; it is an entire sensory shift. The harsh coastal glare dissolves into a cinematic wash of slate-grey skies and emerald foliage so bright it almost glows. When the rain breaks over the roof, the world outside shrinks to the perimeter of your veranda, and the usual travel rush simply ceases to exist. At ZO Hotel, the season isn’t something you watch from a distance — it shapes every quiet, luxurious minute of your day.

The Rain on Terracotta

The mornings start with the heavy, rhythmic drumming of water on ancient clay roof tiles. The scent of petrichor — wet, mineral-rich red Goan soil mingling with crushed wild ferns — drifts in the moment you unlatch the wooden louvers. Instead of chasing beach shacks, your morning begins wrapped in washed linen sheets, watching droplets slide down palm fronds the size of oars.

Downstairs, the brass kettle is always simmering. A steaming glass of lemon-grass chai, sweetened with dark local jaggery, warms your hands while the wind whips the garden into a frenzy. You sit on deep, cushioned wicker chairs on the covered porch, a woven throw over your lap, watching the courtyard turn into a mirror of rainwater.

Warm Kitchens and Wet Roads

When the downpour eases to a soft, misty drizzle, the lanes outside call. You slip into sandals, grab an umbrella from the brass stand by the door, and wander down village lanes lined with crumbling Portuguese villas. The air is cool, completely stripped of summer heat.

Return to the smell of roasted spices drifting from the kitchen. Monsoon meals here are built for comfort: hot, crispy rava-fried fish fresh from the local market, bowls of steaming fish curry spiced with sour kokum, and crusty poi bread still warm from the baker’s basket. Every bite cuts straight through the cool, damp afternoon air.

Evenings by the Amber Glow

Dusk falls early under heavy clouds, turning the hotel into a warm, amber refuge against the dark storm outside. Rain lashes against the French doors, but inside, the floorboards are dry, jazz hums softly from the speakers, and a glass of spiced feni or dark rum sits sweating on a timber coaster.

Guests gather naturally in the common lounge, swapping damp rain jackets for dry socks, drawn together by the hypnotic, steady roar of thunder across the canopy. You talk late into the night, or read by the glow of a reading lamp, knowing there is nowhere else you need to be.

Goa in the sun belongs to everyone. Goa in the rain belongs only to those who know how to slow down and listen.

Monsoon rates run June to September. Every monsoon booking can be moved once, free, right up to the day of arrival.
